context:
Goal: one uniform direction for every watch, wake and hook (your item 180).
Problem (rule): you asked whether these still exist and use a Claude token. Yes. On main, settings.json runs five as command hooks that call a model: call_judge, prose_judge, reply_judge, feedback_guard and report_guard. sendmessage_state uses the same call. Each starts its own `claude -p`, 25 to 70 s, with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, through one home, decision_watch.invoke_model. local_time makes no model call. None uses Claude Code's built-in prompt hook. How often each one fires is unmeasured.
Based on (read): claude-settings main 446f2d3d: settings.json, hooks/decision_watch.py invoke_model, hooks/local_time.py (read 07:55 CST).
Based on (assumed): Claude Code's built-in prompt hook covers these events and runs on the session's own sign-in, with no token. A lane proves that per event before any move.
Departs from: main (six callers start their own claude -p with a token) — option a moves each one it can to a built-in prompt hook.

lastAnswer.note: do these still exist and are used? these use a claude auth token right? i thought we moved to all being hooked

options.gain: No separate token or process for most of them; one way of hooking.
options.how: Keep invoke_model only where the built-in hook cannot serve the event, with a stated cost.
options.label: Move each to a built-in prompt hook where the event allows
options.lose: A lane per hook group; a built-in hook may judge differently, so each one's tests must pass again.

options.how: One Cost line in invoke_model's record.
options.label: Keep them as they are, and state their cost
options.lose: The token and the extra processes stay.

options.how: Count each hook's fires for one week; delete any with none.
options.label: Measure for a week, then delete the ones that never fire
options.lose: A week of waiting; nothing moves until then.
